title: PDFTranscriber Core Definitions
description: Shared `$defs` for PDFTranscriber document schemas. PDFTranscriber output is always page-based: a transcription run plus an ordered array of physical pages, each carrying body elements and footnotes. These definitions capture that common, page-level layer; document-type schemas (journal-article, book, …) reference them and add their own top-level shape. This file is a definitions library and is not a standalone document schema.

documentMetadata.description: Information about the transcription run. Entirely optional: the whole object, and any field within it, may be omitted or deleted (e.g. for privacy) without affecting the validity of the document.

sourceFile.description: Filename of the source PDF (basename, not a full path).

totalPages.description: Number of pages that were transcribed.

processingDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) of when transcription ran.

modelUsage.description: Map of "provider/model" to the number of API calls made with that model.

frontMatter.description: The work's own front matter as printed: title, optional subtitle, and the people responsible for it. This describes the document's content, as distinct from `documentMetadata`, which describes the transcription run. Every field is optional and the whole object may be omitted — captured here (rather than as body `elements`) so that bibliographic information has one reliable location and can be deleted freely without disturbing the page structure. Used both at the top level of a document and, in collected/edited works, on an individual division (e.g. a chapter author). A footnote attached to the front matter (e.g. an author's acknowledgement note, often marked '*') is anchored from these fields with an inline [^fn-NNNN] reference and stored as an ordinary footnote object on the page where it is printed; such notes are thus distinguishable from numbered body footnotes by the origin of their reference.

title.description: Title of the work or division. May contain inline Markdown (**bold**, *italic*), <sc>small caps</sc> tags, and inline footnote references ([^fn-NNNN]).

subtitle.description: Subtitle, if any. May contain inline Markdown and footnote references.

authors.description: Authors in the order printed. May be empty or omitted. On an edited volume the volume-level authors are usually empty (see `editors`) while each chapter division carries its own authors.

editors.description: Editors in the order printed (e.g. the editors of a collected volume). May be empty or omitted.

person.description: A named contributor — an author or editor.

name.description: Name as printed, in natural mixed case. May contain <sc> tags and inline footnote references ([^fn-NNNN]). A note printed as a starred/daggered footnote is anchored here, with the note itself stored as a footnote object on the page where it is printed.

affiliation.description: Institutional affiliation as printed, if given. Contributors who share an affiliation each carry their own copy. May contain inline footnote references.

id.description: Unique monotonic ID. Format: page-NNNN (zero-padded to at least 4 digits).

pageLabel.description: User-readable page label as printed on the physical page. Not necessarily unique across the document.

runningHeader.description: Running header text if present. Omitted (absent) when there is none.

elements.description: Body elements (paragraphs, headings, block quotes) in reading order. May be empty.

footnotes.description: Footnotes in reading order. May be empty.

skipped.description: true if the page could not be transcribed and was recorded as a placeholder.

skipReason.description: Human-readable error description. Only present when skipped is true.

text.description: May contain inline Markdown (**bold**, *italic*), <sc>small caps</sc> tags, and inline footnote references of the form [^<footnote-id>] (e.g. [^fn-0003]) marking where a footnote is anchored in the running text. A reference points to a footnote's `id` (not its `marker`, which need not be unique); the symbol displayed at that point is the referenced footnote's `marker`.

continuesFromPrevious.description: true if this paragraph continues the preceding paragraph rather than starting a new (indented) one. The interruption may be a page boundary (the previous paragraph is the last element of the preceding page) or an intervening element on the same page, such as a block quote. When false, this paragraph begins a new logical paragraph.

continuesToNext.description: true if this paragraph's text is continued by a following paragraph — whether on the next page or after an intervening element such as a block quote on the same page.

level.description: Heading level for in-body section headings. 1 is the top-most section level, 2 a subsection, etc. The document's own title belongs in `frontMatter.title`, not in a heading.

text.description: May contain inline Markdown formatting and inline footnote references (see `paragraph.text`).
May contain inline Markdown formatting, <sc> tags, and inline footnote references (see `paragraph.text`).

continuesFromPrevious.description: true if this block quote continues a block quote interrupted by a page boundary or an intervening element.

continuesToNext.description: true if this block quote is continued by a following block quote across a page boundary or an intervening element.

id.description: Unique monotonic ID. Format: fn-NNNN. This is the target of inline [^fn-NNNN] references in element text.

marker.description: Footnote marker as displayed in the source (e.g. "1", "*", "†"). Not necessarily unique. A footnote split across a page boundary repeats the marker on its continuation fragment.

text.description: May contain inline Markdown formatting and inline footnote references (see `paragraph.text`).

continuesFromPrevious.description: true if this footnote continues from the previous page.

continuesToNext.description: true if this footnote continues on the next page.
